sources.section: Optimisation levels, inlining and link time
sources.entry: ThinLTO - Defines the thin link, summaries analysed whole-program then parallel backends, and the cache for incremental rebuilds.

summary.title: ThinLTO
summary.one_liner: ThinLTO is a scalable, incremental form of link-time optimization in which the link reads only module summaries for whole-program analysis, then runs parallel backends, and a cache speeds up rebuilds.
takeaways: ThinLTO embeds a compact summary in each bitcode module; the link step merges only summaries, then backends optimize modules in parallel, including function importing.
Enable it with -flto=thin at compile and link (with lld-link, only at compile step), and it works with gold, ld64, and lld.
Control backend thread count with linker-specific options such as jobs=N, -threads=N, or --thinlto-jobs=N.
Incremental builds rely on a linker-specific cache directory option, and cache size and expiry can be limited with a cache policy string.
summary.summary: This LLVM/Clang documentation page introduces ThinLTO, explaining how it differs from monolithic LTO: the compile step emits bitcode with summaries, the link step merges only those summaries into a combined index, and the optimizing backends run in parallel. It gives usage commands for clang and lld-link, lists supported linkers (gold, ld64, lld) with the versions that added support, and documents how to set backend parallelism and enable a build cache. It also covers cache pruning policy options (size, file count, expiry, interval), bootstrapping clang with ThinLTO via CMake, and Integrated Distributed ThinLTO (DTLTO) with its command-line options.
